subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos 12° + cos 84° + cos 132° + cos 156° = −1/2.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 9, book p.84. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The two marks sit on the sum-to-product step and on the closing substitution; the opening pairing stays on the page as unmarked working. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1-Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, and Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. NUMERIC CHECK before authoring: the sum was evaluated to 12 decimal places as −0.500000000000, which is exactly −1/2. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Pair the four terms
steps.margin_note: Take the first with the third, and the second with the fourth. Any other pairing leaves angles with no exact value.

recall.must_convey: That the four terms are paired as (12°, 132°) and (84°, 156°).
accept: pair twelve with one thirty two and eighty four with one fifty six
group the first with the third and the second with the fourth
twelve and one thirty two okati, eighty four and one fifty six inkoti
make two pairs before using the formula

steps.why: The first term is paired with the third and the second with the fourth. Only this pairing gives half-differences of 60° and 36°, which are angles with exact values.
common_mistakes: Pairing the terms in the printed order 12° with 84°.
Trying to work out each cosine as a decimal.
steps.memory_tip: Skip one term each time: 12° with 132°, then 84° with 156°.

steps.label: Apply cos C + cos D
steps.margin_note: First mark. Half-sums are 72° and 120°; half-differences are 60° and 36°. cos(−θ) = cos θ, so the sign of the half-difference does not matter.
lines: cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2)

recall.must_convey: That cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2) is applied to both pairs.
accept: cos c plus cos d is two cos half the sum into cos half the difference
the first pair gives two cos seventy two cos sixty
the second pair gives two cos one twenty cos thirty six
sum to product formula rendu pairs meeda apply cheyyali
convert each pair into a product of cosines
reject: cos thirty six is root five plus one by four

steps.why: The sum-to-product formula turns each pair into a product, and the half-differences 60° and 36° are exactly the angles whose cosines are known.
common_mistakes: Using the cos C − cos D formula, which brings in sines.
Halving only the sum and forgetting to halve the difference.
steps.memory_tip: Half the sum sits in the first cosine, half the difference in the second.

steps.label: Substitute the exact values
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 2 cos 60° = 1 and 2 cos 120° = −1, so the sum is cos 72° − cos 36°. The two square roots cancel and −2/4 remains.

recall.must_convey: That cos 60° = 1/2 and cos 120° = −1/2 reduce the sum to cos 72° − cos 36°, which is −1/2.
accept: two cos sixty is one and two cos one twenty is minus one so it becomes cos seventy two minus cos thirty six
cos seventy two is root five minus one by four and cos thirty six is root five plus one by four
the root five terms cancel and minus two by four is left
root five cancel ayipoyi minus half vasthundi
the answer is minus one by two
reject: convert each pair into a product of cosines

steps.why: The 2 in front cancels against cos 60° = 1/2 and against cos 120° = −1/2, leaving cos 72° − cos 36°. The √5 terms then cancel and only −2/4 is left.
common_mistakes: Swapping the values of cos 36° and cos 72°.
steps.memory_tip: cos 36° is the larger value (√5 + 1)/4 and cos 72° the smaller (√5 − 1)/4; their difference is −2/4.
